newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Commonwealth plans no further rate change.
newsitem.headline: Commonwealth plans no further rate change.

text.p: Commonwealth Bank of Australia (CBA) said on Tuesday it does not plan any further cut in its housing or business lending rates.

Earlier, CBA rival Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd cut its mortgage rates again from Friday's cut of 25 basis points. "No we believe we have a competitive offer," Commonwealth spokeswoman Lyndell Fraser told Reuters.
The Reserve Bank cut official cash rates by 50 basis points to 5.5 percent on Friday. CBA was the first major bank to cut lending rates after the RBA move, but only by 25 basis points.
Following CBA's move on Friday, its three major rivals ANZ, Westpac Banking Corp and National Australia Bank Ltd cut mortgage and business rates by the same margin.
The major banks were later accused by politicians of as colluding on setting rates.

The move also prompted the anti-monopoly authority, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC), to ask the four major banks to explain why they moved so quickly to cut their standard mortgage rates by the same amount.
On Tuesday, ANZ cut its key mortgage interest rate again to 6.99 percent from 7.20 percent, after having cut it from 7.55 percent on Friday after the official rate cut.
